headline: Geometric interface conditioning is extending biomolecular design beyond sequence alone
label: Geometry Conditioned Biomolecular Design
summary: Recent RNA, all-atom, and ligand design preprints and papers condition generation on explicit structural geometry or closed-loop feedback.
synthesis: The dominant thread is conditioning learned design on explicit geometry at the level of biomolecular partners rather than sequence alone. RiboBridge separates RNA conformation generation from protein-RNA assembly using cross-frame interaction geometry, evaluated on a 124-complex benchmark. RiboDFM applies backbone-conditioned discrete flow matching to RNA sequence design, reporting high sequence recovery and self-consistency. Astrolabe extends this logic to all-atom design through closed-loop coordination of sequence proposals with structural intervention. FragDockRL and AbOptimizer are reinforcement learning search frameworks over building-block assembly with tethered docking and multisite sequence editing, so they share the design-search framing more than the geometric conditioning. What is new is geometric representation serving as the conditioning interface, with Astrolabe adding closed-loop structural feedback.
